prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures the 3D layout of a dark outdoor walkway bordered by a tall building wall on the center-right (roughly 4–10 m away), a low planter with shrubs and cats ahead on the left (3–5 m away), a tree and parked car further down the street on the left (15–30 m away), and a person with a bicycle in the bottom-right foreground (1–2 m away, about 2–4 m right of the planter). In frame 1, the foreground person is partly out of view at the bottom-right edge within ~1–1.5 m (near or within arm's reach of the camera wearer) with an arm extended left, drops mostly out of frame in frames 2–4 with only the handlebars/wheel within their own arm's reach, and reappears more fully on the right at ~1.5–2 m in frame 5 as the camera wearer turns right. From RGB and depth together, the person stands to the right of the camera wearer facing forward-left toward the planter rather than looking at the camera wearer, partially occluding a vertical pole (~3–4 m behind them) and the building wall in frames 4–5. Compared to the very dark RGB strip, the depth map makes the foreground person's silhouette, their outstretched arm in frame 1, the vertical pole in frames 4–5, and the receding ground and wall planes much easier to see. However, the depth map is unreliable for small details—merging the cats into the planter blobs, blurring the boundary between the person and their bicycle, and flattening the distant street and sky into uniform black.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map is almost entirely blank across the 5 frames, detecting only a small cyan 'car' mask in the far-left background (~25–30 m away, behind the tree) in frame 1 and a 'person' mask in the lower-right foreground (~1.5–2 m away) in frame 5. Using the RGB context, this person is positioned on the right side of the walkway within roughly 1–2 m of the camera wearer and 2–4 m from the planter on the left, facing and looking forward-left away from the camera wearer with their hands within arm's reach of their bicycle handlebars. Across frames 1–4, the person and bicycle are heavily cropped at the bottom-right border and go completely undetected until the camera turns right in frame 5, bringing the person's upper body into view. While the map helps confirm the presence of the distant occluded car in frame 1 and highlights the dark foreground person in frame 5 that is dim in the RGB image, it provides almost no scene layout on its own. It is highly unreliable in this low-light scene, missing the person in frames 1–4, failing to segment the bicycle, cats, planter, trees, and buildings in any frame, and splitting the person region in frame 5 into coarse, blocky brown and pink masks that bleed into the right frame edge.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is completely black across all 5 frames, failing to detect any body or hand skeletons anywhere in the scene. Relying on the RGB and depth context, a single person is actually present 1–2 m away in the bottom-right foreground (near the camera wearer's arm's reach and about 2–4 m from the planter and cats on the left), heavily cropped by the bottom-right frame boundary in frames 1–4 before coming into clearer view on the right in frame 5 as the camera turns right. In the RGB strip, this person extends an arm left in frame 1 and by frame 5 stands facing and looking forward-left with both hands within arm's reach of and resting on their bicycle handlebars, never facing or looking toward the camera wearer. Because no yellow body or magenta hand keypoints are rendered, the pose map reveals nothing that is hard to see in the RGB image. The map is entirely unreliable here, as severe nighttime darkness and partial frame-edge occlusion cause complete missed detections across all five frames.
